# Contributing to AlienCore

Thanks for your interest in AlienCore.

**AlienCore is commercial, source-available software** — not open source. The repository is public so you can audit what runs on your machine, verify release integrity, and see exactly what each setting does. It is not a community project, and **outside pull requests are not accepted at this time.**

## What you can do instead

### Report a bug

[Open an issue](https://github.com/mourninggrace/AlienCore/issues/new) with:

- AlienCore version (`Settings → About` or the title bar)
- Windows version (10 / 11) and build number
- Hardware: CPU model, GPU model, laptop brand if applicable
- What you did, what happened, what you expected
- Relevant lines from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AlienCore\logs\aliencore.log` if the issue is reproducible

The more specific the report, the faster the fix.

### Request a feature

Open an issue and label it `enhancement`. Good ideas land on the roadmap; not all of them ship. Be specific about *what problem you're trying to solve* — that's far more useful than a proposed implementation.

### Get help using the app

- **User manual** — open Settings and click *User Manual* in the bottom-left footer; the full feature walkthrough lives there.
- **Email support** — [mourning.grace.2014@gmail.com](mailto:mourning.grace.2014@gmail.com) for licensing, billing, or anything you'd rather not post publicly.
- **Public Q&A** — [open an issue](https://github.com/mourninggrace/AlienCore/issues/new) tagged `question`.

## Reporting a security vulnerability

Please do **not** open a public issue for security bugs. Email [mourning.grace.2014@gmail.com](mailto:mourning.grace.2014@gmail.com) with `[security]` in the subject line and as much detail as you can share — repro steps, affected version, suspected impact. You'll get an acknowledgement within a few days. If you'd like credit for the find, you can be named in the release notes for the version that fixes it.

## What happens to pull requests

PRs from outside the project will be closed without review. This isn't personal — it's the licensing model. The source is visible so you can see what AlienCore does on your machine; the right to modify and redistribute the source is not part of the license. See [LICENSE](../LICENSE) for the actual legal terms.

If you have an idea for an improvement, the right channel is an issue with a clear description, not a code drop.

Thanks for understanding.
